highlights:
Red flags (2):

- Outreach prices partly did not match any observed live ask (RTX 4090 $0.70, B200 $5.64, H100 SXM $1.70)
- Many third-party reviews from October-November 2026 are paid, affiliate or supporter placements

## // Review

by the bestcloudmining editorial desk · curated review · prose updated 2026-11-04 · facts as of 2026-11-04 · how we verify

...

Lium exposes live prices, fleet counts and launch success rates without an account [2] [3] [13]. A single validator operated by the Lium team checks every connected node every 15 minutes [12]. The public validator source shows that all emission slots the docs label burn route to UID 47, the Datura payout key [9]. An independent analysis notes that the billing endpoint began requiring a validator signature on 7 October 2026, so outside revenue checks are harder now [10]. Proof is therefore partial: hardware checks and optional attestation exist, but machine scores and payouts rest on the operator's own validator [9] [12].

...

## Pricing

Providers set their own prices, so asks move by the minute [2]. Lowest live asks per GPU-hour on the check date: RTX 3090 $0.16, RTX 4090 $0.40, RTX 5090 $0.50, A100 SXM4 80GB $1.68, H100 PCIe $1.79, H100 80GB HBM3 $2.08, H200 $3.60, B200 $5.88 and B300 $6.80 [2]. On consumer cards Vast.ai was cheaper in the sponsored test: an RTX 5090 from $0.40 against Lium's $0.71 [14]. Persistent volumes cost $0.00005 per GB-hour, about $0.036 per GB-month, plus egress [16].

Lium's Secure tier cost less than Lambda's on-demand instances on every GPU in the table below, and Lium also offers on-demand 8x H200 NVLink nodes. All prices below were read on 29 October 2026 at 15:08 UTC. Lium is a marketplace where independent providers set their own prices, so these asks move during the day; Lambda's on-demand instance rates are charged plus applicable sales tax, VAT, or GST. Sources: Lium's public node feed and lambda.ai/pricing. Prices are per GPU per hour.

highlights:
# GPU Rental Price Index: October 2026.

What renting an H100, H200, A100, L40S or RTX 4090 actually cost in October 2026: market and cheapest hourly prices from 190,660 listings, and what moved.

 By Vi Nguyen · Published November 1, 2026 · Prices on this page are live · Editorial policy 

GPUs in the index 15 190,660 price readings collected in October 2026

Median change vs previous month +13.3% market price, across the 15 GPUs with a prior month

## The numbers

The market price is what a typical provider charged for one GPU per hour — the median across providers, day by day, over the month. The cheapest column is the lowest-priced provider over the same month, which is what you'd pay if you shopped around and were flexible about where you rent. Both are medians of daily values, so a single promotional or mispriced listing doesn't move them.

## What moved in October 2026

- Biggest rise: the Nvidia H200, up 64.3%.
- 1 of 15 GPUs moved by less than 3% — a month where most prices shifted noticeably.

...

Use the market price to budget, and the cheapest price as the floor you can reach with some shopping. Neither is a quote: marketplace prices move by the hour, which is why every GPU name above links to its live page with today's prices by provider. For a model-first view, the VRAM fit calculator lists every card that can run a given model with its current cheapest price.

The basket is fixed so months stay comparable.

...

For each GPU we take every listing collected during the month, compute each provider's daily median hourly price, then the median across providers for each day (the market price) and the lowest provider (the cheapest price). The monthly figure is the median of those daily values.

results.title: H100 Rental Prices in 2026: Lium vs RunPod vs Vast.ai vs CoreWeave vs Big Cloud | CloudMart Blog
highlights:
## H100 80GB: single-GPU prices

| Provider | On-demand /hr | Spot /hr | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lium | $1.70 | - | Marketplace, priced per GPU-hour by node, billed by the second |
| Crusoe | $3.90 | - | Flat rate, no interruption risk |
| RunPod | $3.99 | $1.99 | Per-second billing, Secure + Community tiers |
| Lambda Labs | $4.89 | - | ML-focused tooling, flat rate |
| CoreWeave | $6.16 | $2.46 | InfiniBand interconnect, built for clusters |
| Microsoft Azure | $98.32 | $18.17 | ND96isr H100 v5, enterprise integration |

> Prices are per GPU-hour, pulled from the CloudMart GPU marketplace each time this page loads and sorted by price - they're current as you read this, not as of publication. Marketplace providers move continuously through the day.

...

Lium and Vast.ai are marketplaces. You rent a specific node from a specific host, and the price depends which node you get. All Lium prices here are per GPU-hour; their H100s currently run $1.70-$2.90/GPU-hr depending on availability, and the low end is the cheapest node online right now rather than a rate card - it moves through the day as capacity is rented and released. Billing is by the second with no contract or minimum, and they expose a CLI, SDK, API and an MCP server, which makes Lium unusually easy to drive from an agent rather than a dashboard.

...

And if you're doing inference on a quantized 7B-13B model, you may not need datacenter GPUs at all: an RTX 4090 24GB runs varies/hr on Vast.ai and $0.89/hr on RunPod. Lium lists RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell - 96GB of VRAM - from $1.70 per GPU-hour, which is a lot of memory for the money if your model is memory-bound rather than compute-bound. 

## Newer silicon: H200, B200, B300

 Blackwell has reached the independents, and it is no longer quote-only. Lium currently lists H200 141GB from $3.80, B200 180GB from $6.45, and B300 288GB from $5.00 - all per GPU-hour, billed by the second. These are marketplace rates and move with availability; the live listing carries current figures. 

 Whether they're worth it depends entirely on whether you're memory-bound. For a model that spills out of 80GB and forces you into multi-GPU sharding, compare a single 141GB H200 at $3.80 against 2× H100 at $3.40. That's close enough that the simpler single-card setup usually wins on both throughput and engineering time.
